description: Approved npm audit exceptions, evaluated by scripts/audit-policy.mjs (CI frontend job, step 'Full dependency audit'). Each exception accepts exactly one advisory in exactly the recorded dev-only dependency chain until its review deadline; anything else in the full audit fails the gate. Exceptions may share dependent packages (R102 and R144 since 2026-11-17): a shared package must be reported at an approved severity of one of the advisories it resolves to. npmReportedRange may be exactly "*" (npm's form when no patched release exists); vulnerableRange must always be a literal range. A passing evaluation is a policy-based acceptance, NOT a clean npm audit: the full report keeps listing the accepted advisory. Production dependencies are audited separately with no exceptions (npm audit --omit=dev). See docs/reports/phase-6-ci-security-policy.md.

exceptions.title: minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
exceptions.justification: Development tooling only: the one vulnerable copy (minimatch 10.2.6 under @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree) is reached only through typescript-eslint and the @typescript-eslint packages, which lint the repository's own files with the repository's own config globs and never match untrusted patterns. npm audit --omit=dev reports 0, npm ls minimatch --omit=dev is empty and no minimatch code is in the production build. GitHub revised this advisory on 2026-11-04: the affected range narrowed from <11.0.1 to >=7.0.0 <11.0.1 and npm's source ID changed from 1244012 to 1244623. That is a metadata revision, not a fix: minimatch 10.2.6 stays vulnerable. minimatch 3.1.5 (still installed, dev-only) is outside THIS advisory's range, which says nothing about any other vulnerability in 3.x. npm reports the same interval in two forms, so the advisory range (vulnerableRange) and the finding entry's range (npmReportedRange) are recorded and checked separately and exactly. The only patched line is the new major minimatch 11.x (11.0.1 of 2026-10-27), outside the range typescript-estree declares (^10.2.x); npm's suggested fix is a semver-major change of eslint-config-next (15.5.29), so neither npm audit fix --force nor an override is applied. Since 2026-11-17 every package of this chain is also reached by GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch, R144); npm then reports one severity per package (moderate or high), and the gate accepts only an approved severity of the advisories the package resolves to. R144 does not widen this exception: its chain, copies and fields are checked separately. Re-reviewed 2026-11-18 (user decision, docs/reports/phase-8h-ci.md §10): typescript-eslint 8.73.0 (2026-11-16T17:07Z, outside the advisory range) satisfies eslint-config-next's ^8.56.0, so npm audit with current registry metadata (CI, empty cache) no longer reports eslint-config-next through typescript-eslint; it was removed from this chain and remains a dependent of R144 only. A report built from stale cached registry metadata still lists that edge and fails this gate.
exceptions.approvedBy: Architectural review of docs/reports/phase-6-final-qa.md (temporary dev-only exception)
exceptions.remediation: Eliminate every R102 finding through compatible patched upstream dependencies: upgrade typescript-eslint (@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree) and eslint-config-next to releases that depend on minimatch >= 11.0.1, confirm that the full npm audit no longer reports GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, then delete this exception. Until the advisory revision of 2026-11-04 the minimatch 3.1.5 copy was also in scope (through eslint, @eslint/config-array, @eslint/eslintrc, eslint-plugin-import, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y and eslint-plugin-react); the revision narrowed the currently accepted exposure to the 10.x chain and remediated nothing. If no such release exists by the deadline, the exception must be re-reviewed; it is not renewed automatically.
blockingConditions: any advisory not accepted by an exception in this policy (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 here; GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf only under R144), at any severity, in any dependency
any finding whose underlying advisory cannot be resolved to a GitHub advisory ID
any vulnerable node that is not dev-only in package-lock.json
GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 with a different severity, advisory range (vulnerableRange), npm entry range (npmReportedRange), CWE, npm source ID or title
any change to the vulnerable minimatch copies (node paths or installed versions)
any change to the set of dependent packages, their node paths or their direct/transitive status
the review deadline (end of 2026-11-30 UTC) has passed
a missing, malformed or incomplete policy, audit report or lockfile, or an npm audit execution failure

exceptions.title: picomatch vulnerable to ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs
exceptions.justification: Development tooling only. picomatch 2.3.2 is reached through eslint-config-next -> @next/eslint-plugin-next -> fast-glob -> micromatch, and picomatch 4.0.7 through eslint-import-resolver-typescript and @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree -> tinyglobby (and fdir). These lint the repository's own files with the repository's own config globs and resolve its own import paths; they never match untrusted patterns, and the ReDoS needs an attacker-supplied glob such as +(*). npm audit --omit=dev reports 0, npm ls picomatch --omit=dev is empty and no picomatch code is in .next/static. GitHub revised the advisory on 2026-11-17T15:56Z to picomatch <=4.0.7 with no patched version; npm therefore writes the finding entry's range as "*" (every published version), which this exception records exactly (npmReportedRange). npm's suggested fix is a semver-major downgrade of eslint-config-next to 14.2.35, so neither npm audit fix --force nor an override is applied. The chain overlaps R102 (typescript-eslint and the five @typescript-eslint packages); each exception is checked against its own advisory.
exceptions.approvedBy: User decision of 2026-11-17 (docs/reports/phase-8h-ci.md §8-§9; temporary dev-only exception)
exceptions.remediation: Remove every GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf finding once picomatch publishes a release outside <=4.0.7 that meets the two-week rule (or is adopted under a reviewed security exception): move the 4.x copy (tinyglobby, fdir) and the 2.x copy (micromatch, which needs picomatch ^2.3.1) to patched releases through compatible upgrades or exact overrides, confirm that the full npm audit no longer reports the advisory, then delete this exception. If no patched release exists by the deadline, the exception must be re-reviewed; it is not renewed automatically.
